IMPDH1 causes RP10, an autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa locus on chromosome 7q31.3. RP2 and RPGR are both causative genes for X-linked retinitis pigmentosa. A multipoint linkage analysis in 20 X-linked RP families is directly relevant to identifying and characterizing the RP2 and RPGR loci. This is foundational genetic mapping work for both genes.

GUCA1A encodes GCAP1 and GUCA1B encodes GCAP2 (guanylate cyclase activating proteins), which are the direct physiological activators of GUCY2D (retinal guanylate cyclase 2D). A review of guanylate cyclase-activating proteins structure, function, and diversity is directly on-topic for three of the four listed genes (GUCA1A, GUCA1B, GUCY2D). GPR143 (OA1) causes X-linked ocular albinism and is directly implicated in aberrant retinal axon guidance at the optic chiasm. This paper's focus on chiasmatic misrouting in albinism is GPR143's core phenotypic territory. FRMD7 causes congenital nystagmus, which is a common consequence of the chiasmatic misrouting and foveal hypoplasia described here. The paper covers both genes' phenotypic overlap directly.

GJA3 encodes connexin 46 (Cx46) and GJA8 encodes connexin 50 (Cx50), both of which cause congenital cataracts when mutated. The paper is directly on-topic for GJA3 and GJA8 disease mechanisms.

This is directly relevant clinical literature for the condition caused by FRMD7 mutations.

GUCY2D encodes the photoreceptor retinal guanylate cyclase (ROS-GC1/RETGC-1). This paper investigates the calcium-dependent stimulation of membrane-bound guanylate cyclase activity in bovine retina by S100B and S100A1. The 'membrane-bound guanylate cyclase' studied is GUCY2D itself. While S100 proteins are not the canonical GCAPs (GUCA1A/GUCA1B), this paper directly characterizes the functional regulation of GUCY2D activity in the retina.

This paper characterizes CD-GCAP, a retinal calcium-binding protein that activates ROS-GC (the rod outer segment guanylate cyclase, i.e. GUCY2D) in a calcium-dependent manner, and establishes its identity with S100beta. The paper directly studies the activation mechanism of GUCY2D (ROS-GC) and the calcium-dependent modulation that underlies phototransduction and is disrupted in GUCY2D-associated LCA/cone-rod dystrophy.

GJA8 encodes connexin 50 (Cx50), which causes congenital cataract when mutated. This paper directly studies structure-function relationships of the Cx50 amino-terminal domain using mutations and chimeras, characterizing single-channel conductance and voltage-dependent gating.
